stem: The root system has expanded substantially and containers now reach the same dryback threshold much earlier each day. What change is best supported?
choices: Keep irrigation timing unchanged because the container volume has not changed, so faster dryback should be treated as temporary variation
Increase nutrient concentration because a larger root system primarily increases mineral demand rather than daily water use
Reassess irrigation timing or frequency against faster measured depletion while maintaining an appropriate root-zone air-water balance
Delay irrigation until visible wilting occurs so the larger root system fully uses the stored water before each new event
rationale: As root systems and transpiring canopies develop, water use can increase. Irrigation timing should respond to measured depletion while preserving an appropriate air-water balance.
